deviations: Activity gate: all three engines skip an entity whose last_seen is more than 6 h old. For aggregation and periodicity that is their span. For trend the 12 h span would otherwise still emit for an entity that has been silent 6 to 12 h, which breaks the spec test 'an entity silent for more than 6 h gets no window metrics'.

Trend targets that are not D0 inputs (l4.bytes_up, l4.distinct_peers, http.latency_ms_avg, probe.rtt_ms) get raw retention of 13 h instead of the 6 h default for raw scalars. Without it the first half of the 12 h trend grid is empty or zero-filled, which gives a NaN or false changepoint. This goes beyond contract B's retention table.

Cadence invariance: counter grid values are rescaled to the current tick length (v * dt_now / dt_tick). sum is the true total; mean is the time-weighted rate per current tick; p95, max and cv are taken over the rescaled values. Trend's EWMA uses a 1800 s wall-clock half-life (about v1's alpha 0.3 at 900 s ticks), and its slope is fitted against time and reported per current tick. On a uniform grid all of these equal the plain v1-style statistics.

trend changepoint is now a Welch z of the recent-half mean minus the prior-half mean, split at now - 6 h. Variance is floored at the pooled mean for counters (Poisson) and at (1% of the level)^2 for gauges, and z is clipped to +/-10. v1's robust z against median/MAD gave a saturated +/-6 on sparse series with MAD = 0.

periodicity: act.events was added as a fourth count target, so TLS-only and L4-only automation is covered. The autocorrelation is FFT-based over lags 2 to n/2. When the grid is non-uniform (a cadence switch or a gap inside the span), counts are re-binned at the coarsest spacing, capped at span/8, so beacon_lag in seconds keeps one meaning. timing_regularity is written only when there are at least 2 active ticks. Otherwise it is absent, which B01 reads as NaN.
A target with no raw point in the span is not written, and neither is an all-NaN gauge. This is 'absence is data', not 'zero'.

The engines use fresh.grid_times, plus an equivalent vectorised fill (grid_many), instead of calling fresh.grid once per metric. A test asserts the outputs are identical to fresh.grid; the change was made for performance (fresh.grid's Python loop was about 60% of runtime at 60 s ticks).

Perf: measured about 1.8 ms per entity for all three engines at 900 s ticks and about 5.3 ms per entity at 60 s ticks (a 720-point 12 h grid). The spec's 'at most 3 ms per tick' is met only for small populations. Aggregation's writes alone are 45-65 add_derived calls per entity.

engine: D1 — RatioEngine / EntropyEngine / GraphEngine (derived, interval 1, no period_s
requested: Docs (engines.md D1 or contract B): write down what `derived.<x>_n` means (total set mass including '__other__') and that entropies exclude '__other__'. B01's bounded gate (n >= 5) and B04 read this value, so its meaning should be stated.
Optional: contract B could mention that D1 graph peers now include l4.peer_set buckets and use eTLD+1 names.
deviations: The `_n` value for each entropy output is the total mass of its set, with '__other__' included. Because of R1 this is the true request, query or handshake count. The entropy itself is computed only on the 64 named entries: '__other__' is a remainder, not a category, and counting it as one would make a tunnel with thousands of random names look concentrated. The spec only says 'the number of items', so this is my reading of it.

derived.ja3_diversity counts the named fingerprints, plus 1 when a '__other__' remainder exists. This is a lower bound. derived.dns_dga_score is the count-weighted mean character entropy of the first label over the named qnames. v1 had the same formula, now cached.

Graph peers are TLS and DNS names at eTLD+1, preferring the R1 *_etld1_set series and otherwise mapping the full-name set through names.etld1, plus l4.peer_set buckets (/24, /64 or host). v1 used full SNI and qname names only. Full names would make every random DNS label a 'new peer', and l4.peer_set captures destinations reached without DNS or TLS. '__other__' is never treated as a peer.

derived.fanout is written only when l4.distinct_peers is fresh. v1 fell back to len(peers). new_peer_count is written, and may be 0, whenever at least one peer source is fresh. peer_novelty needs at least one peer.

dest_concentration keeps the v1 source order (tls.sni_set first, then dns.qname_set, full names). It is the top named count divided by the true total with '__other__' included, and is written only when that set is fresh.

The 30-day history {peer: last_seen_ts} is engine-instance memory, as in v1. It is not a contract-C model, so it is not trust-gated or checkpointed through lib/gating. Contract C lists no D1 model and the D1 spec does not ask for gating. The history is swept once a day per entity, capped at max_peers (default 20000; beyond it the newest half is kept), and fully dropped for entities idle longer than the TTL. If the clock goes backwards during replay, a peer seen 'in the future' still counts as known.

Entities are iterated with store.entities_active(system, now), which relies on raw engines touching last_seen when they write real data. The act.events zero-fill uses touch=False, so silent entities are skipped cheaply. The freshness check is still applied to every input.
Constructor keyword parameters (all optional): GraphEngine(peer_ttl_s=30*86400, max_peers=20000).

requested: build.py (not mine): per the spec D2 is order 4, after D0 (order 0) and D1 (order 1). SessionEngine currently sits between EntropyEngine and GraphEngine, which is harmless because D2 reads only act.*, but it should move after the D0 and D1 engines for spec order.

Docs (engines.md D2): state that req_per_session is absent while no session has completed, that duty is time-weighted across cadence changes, and that session counts are not reweighted by stream_frac (only event counts are).
deviations: Duty weights each tick by its wall-clock length: the gap to the previous clock tick, capped at 3600 s so a pipeline outage cannot count as one long tick. At a uniform cadence this equals the fraction of active ticks. After a 900 -> 60 cadence switch, a plain tick count would let the 60 s ticks outvote the 900 s ones.

stream_frac reweighting applies to event counts (the req_per_session numerator, weight 1/frac per row) but not to the session count. R2 drops whole sub-sessions cut at 30 s, far below G (120 s or more), so dropping one almost never removes a whole D2 session. Reweighting the session count would overcount sessions.

Think-time gaps: on a sampled tick (stream_frac < 1) only gaps of 30 s or less are used, because the m_template sampling contract guarantees only those are real gaps between consecutive events; B11 applies the same rule. A gap across the tick boundary counts only when both ticks were unsampled. Gaps of exactly 0 (records sharing one obs.ts) are skipped. A missing or invalid frac is treated as complete rows.

req_per_session is not written, rather than written as 0 or NaN, while no session has completed in the 24 h window: during the first 1–2 ticks, and after 24 h of silence. The spec test's 'window metrics on every tick' holds for duty and session_count on every tick and for req_per_session from the first completed session onward.

Window metrics require R2's act.events clock point at ctx.now (R2 zero-fills every entity seen in the last 30 d), so a stale grid is never re-stamped. An entity with no act.events and no act.stream gets nothing, because there is no fallback to http.requests or l4.flows as v1 had.

Session and clock state lives in memory per engine instance and is updated incrementally, because act.stream is kept for only 1 h while the session window is 24 h. It is not a contract-C model and is not trust-gated, since it is a representation and not a learner of normality. A fresh instance bootstraps duty from 24 h of act.events but sees sessions only from the act.stream still retained. When the clock goes backwards the entity's state is reset, and entities idle for more than 2 d are swept.

deviations: Spec test (a) 'log-normal gaps with sigma = 1 give B in [0.2, 0.6]' cannot hold for a pure log-normal renewal: CV = sqrt(e-1) = 1.31, so B = 0.135 (measured 0.13-0.15). The test implements it with the generator's human persona (think time LogNormal(ln 8 s, 1.0) inside sessions, Exp(300 s) breaks between sessions), which gives B of about 0.37-0.53, inside the range. It also asserts that the pure renewal matches theory (sigma = 1 gives B in [0.08, 0.2]; sigma = 1.3 gives B in [0.2, 0.6]).

B and M use 'active' gaps below 30 min (fixed BURST_MAX_S). The think-time log-normal fit uses within-session gaps below model.seq session_gap, as the spec says. Using all gaps would let one overnight gap dominate B. Using session_gap for B as well, as the interrupted draft did, would drop the between-session breaks that make humans bursty, and B collapses to about 0.09 once B10 learns a ~150-s session gap.

The 'timing p' in spec test (b) is tested on behavior.pm[timing]: a two-sample G test (G = 2N*JSD) divided by a learned per-daypart overdispersion phi, against chi2_df. score.timing is the JSD and is made conformal by B24 as specified. behavior.pm is float32, so pm is floored at 1.18e-38 instead of 1e-300, which would store as 0.

The strict-period check: the rfft of 5-s bins over 2 h picks a candidate (harmonic sum), which is confirmed by the window-corrected Rayleigh statistic Z^2_1 (evt.z2_periodogram, m=1) with evt.z2_p's Davies bound over the scanned band [10 s, span/4]. This accounts for the period search, which a plain rayleigh_p at the chosen period does not. The test also checks evt.rayleigh_p < 1e-4 at the reported period. A period is published only when p <= 1e-3.

The period check uses only events from complete ticks (stream_frac = 1). R2 caps a long session to one contiguous chunk per tick, and the resulting holes produced a false 'strict period' (308 s, p = 2e-7) for a 0.8-s scraper. A sampled tick clears the event buffer.

Reads beyond the spec's list: act.events and last_seen (to tell silence from a missing zero-fill), feature.active (the GatedLearner clock), trust_prov, quarantine and model.link (contract H). Writes beyond the spec's list: behavior.pm, behavior.axes and behavior.degraded (via emit).
A re-run of the same tick is made exact: the pre-tick gap-chain and event-buffer state is snapshotted and restored.

π (the feedback multiplier) is applied per component rather than as one global factor: risk = 100(1 - exp(-M·c_s·Σ π_k L_k / 60)), where π_k = m_feedback.risk_mult(family of the component). Event components use m_feedback.EVENT_FAMILY; lib-4 components use π = 1. It is applied at read time, so a label changes risk immediately without rewriting L.

The spec does not fix these weights or half-lives, so I chose them. xsys weight is 1.5. Half-lives by family: intensity, shape, peer, temporal, breadth and xsys 12 h; change 24 h; sequence 24 h; categorical 72 h (novelty); identity 72 h; c2 48 h; exfil 48 h. By event kind: first_seen, rare_access and class_adoption_risky 72 h (novelty); client_impersonation, identity_mismatch, possible_impersonation and new_entity_unmatched 72 h (identity); beacon 48 h (c2); budget_exceeded 48 h (exfil). By lib-4 stage: c2 and exfiltration 48 h, identity 72 h, everything else 12 h. Any finding of severity critical, and this tick's continuous evidence when behavior.alarm severity is critical, uses 48 h, or the slower class if that is longer.
Repeat damping (0.5^(n-1) within 24 h) also applies to lib-4 matches, keyed by signature_id. Without it, a low-severity signature firing every 60 s would saturate risk.

first_seen tier comes from event.extra['tier'] (system/org -> system; class/role/static/pool/sub -> class; anything else -> entity, weight 3). A first_seen with extra['adopted'] true counts x0.1 (the B08 adoption discount); a numeric extra['discount'] in (0, 1] is applied instead when given. A system- or class-tier first_seen or rare_access is treated as low_prevalence, so its stage is c2 unless its axes or flags refine it; rare_access defaults to sensitive (stage privilege). The repeat key is dedupe_key, else extra token, else dim=value.

Episode definition: each (key, family) has a streak counter. A tick with a valid p and e_day >= 1 resets it unless an open, acked or suppressed incident covers the key (the incident is the episode). A NaN or missing family neither contributes nor resets.
Suppression x0.25: all new evidence counts x0.25 while the key's only live incidents are suppressed; any event with status 'suppressed' also counts x0.25.

State (decayed components, streaks, repeats, stage times, tier, trend history) is kept in memory per store (a WeakKeyDictionary), not in a model: contract C has no risk model. Nothing is learned from live data (L_ref is fixed), so lib/gating and model.control do not apply. A clock that goes backwards resets the key, and re-running the same tick is idempotent.

Contract M: when behavior.fusion has an error at this tick, risk is written as NaN and profile.extra.risk.degraded is set to True. State is left untouched, so the next tick catches up both decay and the discrete windows.

Class risk = nanmax(own, mean of the top 3 finite member risks); with fewer than 3 members it is the mean of those available. System risk = nanmax over entities and classes, written only when the system has at least one key.

The runner could keep snapshots small by storing only m_baseline.anchor_summary per perturbed feature instead of _jsonable(model), which includes gate journals.
deviations: Checkpoints are float32 bucket blocks (zlib-compressed when mostly zero), not float16: float16 overflows the raw moment sums (sum x^2, scaled by 2^(t/H)). Rollback equality is then ~6e-8 relative (test (e) asserts 1e-6 relative). Blocks untouched between checkpoints are shared, and Blob.__deepcopy__ returns self (the blob is immutable).

The rate cap is a per-bucket band-day: day boundaries sit 12 h from the bucket's hour, so one daily cluster of commits is one band. Within a band the bucket's DATA mean sum(num)/sum(den) may move at most +-cap*sigma15, with sigma15 from the bucket's own posterior at the band start. A violating row is folded with the largest weight that lands on the band edge. The data mean is used because decay cannot move it; the posterior mean drifts slightly toward the hyperprior as data ages. A per-row allowance was rejected because it also clips ordinary noise and freezes learning. The cap binds only on bucket-features with >= 8 rows and >= 120 weighted minutes at band start (half of each once capped, as hysteresis), so the hyperprior start converges freely.

bin168 is location-only: 168 cells hold first-order stats that refine the bin48 mean, shrunk with 4 pseudo-rows, while dispersion comes from bin48. The cells are used once commits span >= 28 d, on typical days only; holidays and make-up workdays stay on bin48. The reference anchor is bin48-only with a fixed 28-d half-life.

Two ratio kinds are modelled as Student-t on logit(nat), not Beta-Binomial: retransmit_rate (n = l4.pkts_total) and probe_loss (n = probe.probes), because their exposure is not recoverable from feature.nat/expo. dns_fail_rate uses dns_queries as n (D1 writes its .n from dns.queries). Ratio stats are [W, sum k, sum n, sum k^2/n]; sum (k/n)^2 is dropped because bayes.ratio_posterior does not use it.

Row values are rebuilt from feature.nat (8-d retention), not feature.vec (1-d), so rollback replays are exact. Expo channels come from the nat count features, which are identical to feature.expo. tctx is computed with timebins.tctx_from_config (as B01 does) instead of being read from feature.tctx. A row's exposure is the gap to the previous feature.active tick (<= 3600 s), else ctx.window_s.
Only active ticks (feature.active == 1) are committed, because B04 scores active ticks and absence is B07's job. Inactive ticks still advance the commit cursor.

Tiers (class / system / org) are the sums of their members' current-anchor stats, recomputed hourly, rather than incrementally updated. They therefore follow member rollbacks. Every link is leave-one-out, and the hyperprior is carried with weight h = s*h_parent, so a child with no data gets exactly the parent's predictive mean. kappa units: 15-min exposure rows for counts, trials for ratios, rows for t. The EB default is kappa = 2 when a tier has < 2 children. Tier models hold current stats only; there is no tier reference anchor.

Reference anchor: the current anchor acts as a 4-row prior, so an empty reference equals the current anchor. It steps in hourly batches for all entities in the same tick, or at once on a new control directive. The admission decision is made at first fetch and cached, so replays are stable. Abnormal regimes are behavior.regime.state in {suspect, drifting, rejected, rollback}. Golden is the cell-wise median of up to 4 UTC-weekly reference snapshots, taken when the finished week's max behavior.risk < 30 (no risk data counts as < 30) and reference n_eff >= 96. Once golden exists the reference predictive uses it.

Half-life selection uses global (unbucketed) shadow stats per candidate H. The p5/p95 pinball loss uses moment approximations for NB/BB and exact t quantiles. It is evaluated on every 8th commit, and losses are halved rather than cleared at each 96-commit selection.

deviations: Good–Turing rate test: n is the number of distinct values in the tick, not raw accesses. Within a tick, accesses to one value come in bursts. With raw accesses, p would be about 1/(2T) after T ticks whatever the history, and spec test (a) could not reach p < 1e-3 at 200 ticks.

N1 is the decayed mass of singleton values (values with n_acc == 1), to match the decayed N. The rate test is skipped until the entity has at least 32 committed accesses. With p_new = 0.5 at N = 0, every new entity would otherwise alarm.

Surprisal term: the sum runs over dimensions and takes the most surprising scored value in each one (Σ_d max_v ω_d·w·I/12), not a sum over every value. Without this, one burst of fresh peers or CDN /24s would add up to dozens of findings. Breadth is left to novelty_rate. ω is computed per dimension, falling back to the pooled value below 20 accesses.
The values in the surprisal sum are those new to the entity (including values already sighted but not yet committed) plus class-rare sensitive or admin values with I ≥ 12 bits.

Event gating: the entity-tier first_seen clause uses maturity-weighted bits (ω_d·I ≥ 12), so an explorer's routine discoveries are not each reported. Class-tier and entity-tier events need a mature entity (≥ 100 accesses and ω ≥ 0.5). System-tier first_seen and rare_access are always emitted. At most 5 events per entity-tick; dedupe per (entity, dim, value) for 30 days.

Tier semantics: 'class' means new or rare among peers (class IDF ≥ ln 5 + 1). When the entity has no class, the system stands in. A known but class-rare sensitive value is reported with tier 'class' on rare_access. 'system' needs a mature system tier (at least 1 member and 50 accesses). A sightings ledger stops a second entity from also reading as system-new before the hourly rebuild.

Class and system tiers are rebuilt hourly from the member entity models, so they inherit gating and rollback. They are not updated incrementally. The system base measure is U = 1/V, where V is a per-dimension universe constant (tmpl 4096, ports / names / peers 65536, qtype and cat 256, ctype 1024) or twice the system's distinct values if larger.
The tmpl dimension uses HTTP act.tokens only. TLS, DNS and L4 tokens would double-count the sni / dns / dport dimensions.

Adoption discount is implemented as score = max(score without adopted values, 0.1 × full score). class_adopted is emitted once per value at the class pseudo-entity (s, 'class:<rid>'). First sightings from all entities are gathered in a first pass, so adopters in the same tick count each other.

novelty_rate: a rolling 24 h count of class-rare first sightings, tested against a Gamma–Poisson NB built from committed complete active UTC days, with method-of-moments overdispersion. It needs at least 2 complete days, otherwise it is unscored. acc_alarm fires when e_day(p) ≤ the detector's budget_per_day.

jsd: max over dimensions of the JSD between each decayed window and the profile p_e, plus a rest bin. The 1 h window is evaluated at most every 5 minutes and the 24 h window hourly. Evaluation starts only once the entity has ≥ 100 accesses: immature profiles give JSD ≈ 1, which would poison the rings. Conformal rings (256) plus a GPD tail, scored once the ring has ≥ 32 entries; Bonferroni over the evaluated windows. acc_alarm fires when e_day ≤ budget.

Sensitivity weight w = 1 + [sensitive or admin] + low_prev × h, capped at 3. h = clip(log10(max(4·up, up+down)/1e4)/2, 0, 1). Admin is detected by a path regex, admin ports and lib-4 category 'admin'. When config sensitive_patterns is empty, built-in defaults are used (salary, payroll, passw, secret, credential).
Degradation: any raw producer error on an active tick sets NaN plus degraded for all three detectors. Activity with no categorical data is 'stale:act.tokens'. Silent entities are not scored.

deviations: Count unit is slot-equivalents, not request counts: each tick adds share_s*dt/900*trust. This keeps N_e cadence-invariant (60/900/3600 s) and stops it growing with request volume; with request counts the entity tier would swamp the class backoff and alpha=5 would mean nothing. The share weighting inside S still uses request counts over the last 10 ticks, as the spec says.

S is capped per token at 20 bits: min(20, -log2 p_e). Without the cap, a stack never seen at any tier costs 30-45 bits depending only on tier sizes, and 0.6*S saturates the logistic, so C/I/R stop mattering.
The system tier uses p_s=(c_s+U)/(N_s+1) with U=1/4096. The spec does not give the system base measure; this mirrors m_vocab.

Concurrency C additionally requires that the two stacks interleave (s0 still active after s1's first event). A clean handover within 5 min (browser restart or upgrade) would otherwise set C=1 and push every first mover of a rollout towards client_impersonation, which breaks test (b). NAT and impersonation interleave, so they are unaffected; test (a) fires with C=1.
'New stack' s1 means p(s1|e) < 0.05. The spec does not define it.

Replacement ('s0 absent for longer than its P99 gap') is measured on the entity's ACTIVE clock: dt accumulates only on ticks where the entity has client traffic without s0. Threshold = max(P99, 30 min, 2*dt). Measured on wall time, a workstation's overnight gaps would push P99 to days and client_change would come days late; a silent host has not replaced anything.

p(ja3n | UA family) uses the R3 client.ua_set key 'family/major' (e.g. 'chrome/127') and needs at least 16 slot-equivalents of that UA before it can set I. With a family-only key, every new Chrome major version with a new ja3n would set I=1 and flag rollouts (breaks test b).

R = max(R_class, R_system). Each is the share of the OTHER members / known entities that first used s1 within 7 d, and each is NaN (ignored) with fewer than 2 others. Acquisitions are recorded live, before scoring, so a same-tick rollout counts. They are recorded only once the entity's backoff chain has at least 16 slot-equivalents of evidence, so start-up is not read as a rollout.
With no new stack this tick, risk = sigmoid(0.6*S - 3) (C=I=R=0). With several, the largest per-stack risk is used.

A tick with no usable fingerprinted traffic is not scored (behavior.score/pm stay NaN) and the entity is not counted absent. Scoring also requires N_e+N_c+N_s >= 16 slot-equivalents. When R3 failed this tick: NaN score plus behavior.degraded.

Class tiers are stored inside model.client@(s,'__system__') under 'classes', because contract C gives model.client no class key. The system and class tiers are rebuilt hourly from the committed entity models, so they inherit trust gating and rollbacks.

Event dedupe: client_impersonation fires at most once per (entity, stack) per 24 h. client_change fires once per (s0 -> s1) transition; while not yet emitted it is re-checked every tick, so R can rise into the threshold later.
Scores are still written in training mode, like B11; only events are suppressed.

P(active) is modelled per 15-minute quarter of each bin48/bin168 hour (192/672 cells), not per whole hour. With whole hours, a 40-minute backup could never reach p>=0.95, so spec test (b) could not pass. von Mises smoothing (kappa 4) borrows from the same quarter of neighbouring hours with an adaptive likelihood-ratio weight, so sharp schedule edges are not blurred.

The detectors clip p_hat to [0.02, 0.98] (det_p). The 'third active slot alarms' arithmetic (3 x 4.64 = 13.9 >= 13.7) therefore holds whatever the history length, and one slot can never carry unbounded evidence.
Silence resets to 0 on an eligible active slot, and the alarm fires at s >= ln(ARL slots) (p_eq <= 1/9600).

Schedule shift: the event is emitted when the moved run ends, not earlier. While a run could still be the missed window (<= its duration + tolerance), the reported offhours W is the pre-run value and the 60-s provisional increment waits. An explained move therefore never raises an offhours alarm. A run that does not match reports its full W at once, at most n0+1 slots late, and only right after a machine-like entity missed its window. The 'shift_explained' flag lives in behavior.rhythm, profile.extra.rhythm and the event's extra. behavior.axes stays in the emit format {detector: ['temporal']}, and B25 applies the LOW cap from the schedule_shift event.

Calendar self-healing needs at least 3 active entities and >= 25% of the system, on top of the > 3x usual system level. The whole local day is then treated as a workday (recorded in model.rhythm@(s,'__system__').healed).

Class prior Beta(6 pi_class, 6(1-pi_class)) needs a class with >= 3 members (contract L). Otherwise the prior falls back to the system tier Beta(2 pi_sys, ...) if the system model has >= 2 members, else Jeffreys.

Spec test (b)/(c) fixtures use 28 training days, not 21. A daily job lands in the workday cells only 5 days in 7, and the 3-member system prior pulls toward the pooled rate, so 3 weeks leave p_hat about 0.949 (just below 0.95). Test (b) asserts on p_hat as it was when the slots were scored, not on the model after the miss was learned.

deviations: Common-mode guard is stricter than the spec. I kept the spec's condition that B/peer_median exceed the P99 of its own ratio history, and added a level-q test on log(B/peer_median): the same-phase median and robust scale plus a POT quantile, like z_q. Without a ratio fit it falls back to z_q rescaled by the peers' current level over their usual level. Reason: under a class-wide shift B > z_q holds at every hourly evaluation, so the P99 alone passes 1% of them. With the P99 alone I measured 1 alarming entity in 48 class-entity-days, which is 2x the whole budget. For large peer sets (more than 8), the history peer median includes the entity itself, for cost reasons.

Thresholds are computed in log space. Horizon sums are standardised as log(W + unit), with unit = 1% of the absolute floor, and z_q = exp(median + scale*z) - unit. Standardising on the raw scale let a skewed single-hour-dominated 8-h window give up to 1% null alarm days; in log space it is 0.16%. As a result, 'rescaled by the entity median' for young entities means taking the peers' log (relative) scales.

Scale and tail regularisation beyond the spec:
- Per-phase scales are smoothed over +-2 local hours.
- Weekends, or any day type with fewer than 10 days, use the spread pooled across day types.
- The 7-d scale is at least the rolling-24h log scale / sqrt(7), and the 7-d z_q is at least the normal quantile.
- The GPD xi is shrunk n/(n+30) and clipped to [0, 0.3], and sigma is at least 0.4.
Without these, the ~13 correlated exceedances gave 1-h z_q values up to about 17.

Fits run round-robin once per local day, spread over 12 h and least-recently-served first, rather than every 6 h. Rollback, release, rebase or a link seed forces an immediate refit. Commits are batched every 4 due rows, or when a row has waited 1 h.

Horizons end with the current partial local hour. Tick rows go to the hour of now - dt/2. Breadth quantities are per-local-day distinct increments, so the 7-d breadth value is the sum of daily distinct counts. HLL is used per template, capped at 128 templates per day, with an overflow sketch.

The 'class-rare' test uses R2's act.rare_events membership, else lib/m_vocab.dest_prevalence when that module imports (guarded by try/except ImportError), else m_template.dest_prevalence at or below 0.2, all behind the private _is_rare. Novelty is first-seen by the entity within 7 d, from B13's own map; the map is inherited on a link. Exfil counts external destinations only (names.is_external); a destination R2 never named counts as external.

Extra read: dns.qname_set, which the spec's Reads list omits but which the DNS-label-bytes quantity needs. I compute feature.tctx from config via lib/timebins instead of reading the series, the same way B11 does.

- bytes_up 5 MB
- bytes_down 50 MB
- writes 200
- slots 8
- up_novel 20 MB

Performance misses the spec target of <= 2 ms per tick. The cost goes to the GatedLearner step and checkpoints, emit upserts, and vectorised evaluation of 36 cells.

deviations: Committed-row buffer keeps at most 336 rows, one per 15-minute slot (the newest committed row of each slot). At 900 s this is identical to the spec. At 60 s a plain 336-row buffer would cover only 5.6 h; slots keep about 3.5 days at every cadence, and the update stays order-independent, so release and replay are exact.

Missing data. A column is modelled if it is finite in at least 50% of rows and no single value holds half of its entries (MCD-type fits collapse on ties). Complete buffers follow the spec path: robustcov.c_step_oas, eigen floor, 90% PCs. Buffers with NaN take a one-step EM path: conditional expectation from a pairwise-complete first pass, the C-step used only as an outlier screen at χ²_{p,0.999}, then OAS of the completed rows plus the E-step conditional covariance. Measured reasons: running the C-step on imputed rows gave 1.9% T² false alarms at the 1% level; the EM path gives 1.0% clean and 0.9% with 10% contamination. Complete-case fitting kept only 13 of 52 columns at 3% scattered NaN.

SPE Box parameters are fitted on out-of-sample SPE/θ1 (θ1 = residual trace). The values come from rows committed since the previous fit, scored under that previous model, in a 256-entry ring, and are trimmed on rollback. Bootstrap falls back to the class model's Box, else a two-fold cross-fit. Multi-seed null check at p=52: SPE 1.04%/5.1% and T² 1.15%/5.6% at the 1%/5% levels.

behavior.wh is the Wilson–Hilferty score of q·F (T² after the prediction scaling) rather than of raw T², so a finite-n fit does not bias it (null mean ≈ 0, sd ≈ 1). It is NaN when the Hotelling p is undefined (n_pred ≤ q+1).
Young-entity shrink (nΣ_e + 30Σ_class)/(n+30) is applied to μ as well as Σ, whenever a class model exists (the weight fades as 30/(n+30)); the Hotelling n becomes n_eff + 30.

An ACCEPTED rebase keeps rows before tau at weight 0.25 rather than dropping them, so the new regime dominates without a cold start. Link seeding adds the source's rows only in slots the entity lacks, at half weight.

Release of held rows older than the 6 h zi ring uses an 8-day per-slot archive that keeps only the newest row of each slot. At cadences below 900 s, a rollback whose tau falls mid-slot cannot replay older rows of that one slot. At 900 s it is exact.

deviations: The engine interval is 1, not 96. Window collection has to run every tick because feature.vec and feature.sketch are kept for only 1 day, and a 96 x 900 s stride plus the commit delay D would read rows that are already pruned. The CV fit still runs every 96 ticks or 24 h, with a per-system phase through Engine.entity_due. The first fit runs as soon as at least 2 entities have at least 9 windows each.

LDA is solved as a generalised eigenproblem (scipy eigh) against the OAS-shrunk within scatter. This is equivalent to sklearn's 'eigen' solver with automatic shrinkage. The 'lsqr' solver was not used because it has no transform, and B16/B17 need an LDA space.

EER_hard is the worst pairwise EER of an entity's held-out genuine windows against each of its 3 nearest impostors, taken separately. Pooling the 3 impostors' windows gives about 0.25 for an identical twin, which would fail the spec's EER > 0.3 assertion.
Bhattacharyya nearest impostors are computed on diagonal Gaussians in the full-data WCCN-whitened PCA space. The LDA space overfits twin separation in-sample.
T99 is the 99th percentile of held-out genuine squared distance d^2 in LDA space. recall@K uses K = 4 candidate ranks.

Non-gauss modality calibration (vocab, rhythm, seq, client, timing) uses live window samples. Raw sets are kept for only 1 h, so B15 cannot rescore old windows. Up to 3 active, non-quarantined entities at a time accumulate the LLR of their raw evidence over K active ticks, under their own model and their 3 nearest impostors' models, through the owners' accessors. The ring holds 2000 samples per modality. These samples are gated by quarantine only and are not reversed by rollback. This adds reads of act.tokens, act.stream, act.stream_frac, client.stack_set, tls.sni_etld1_set, dns.qname_etld1_set and l4.dport_set, which are not in the spec's Reads list.

Per-modality LLR is defined against a background: vocab against the system tier; seq against the system PPM; client against the system tier; rhythm against the system rhythm model, or else the mean p over entity models; timing against the mean pmf over entity models. The gauss background is a full Gaussian of all windows in LDA space. When a logistic slope comes out below 0, calibration is set to (0, 0). The default is (1, 0) until there are 20 samples of each label.
'log think_mu' is taken as behavior.timing.think_mu as is, because B11 already stores the mean of ln(gap).

Modality-drop importance, run every 4th fit, uses 9 blocks: volume, breadth, app, dns_tls, timing (feature timing group plus behavior.timing), transport (+probe), comp, sketch and clock. The pooled PCA basis is not refitted per block; the block's standardised and mask columns are zeroed before projection, and WCCN/LDA are refitted in every fold. This saves 9 eigendecompositions.
Class identifiability covers role classes from model.class only, not static or pool classes. It needs at least 2 roles among the scored entities.

Held rows older than feature.vec's 1-day retention cannot be released or replayed, so they are skipped. Ticks with trust below 0.5 are not learned (a binary weight). Link seeding adds every second window of the linked entity A to B, still pointing at A's stored vectors.

low_identifiability is emitted once per crossing above 0.2 and re-armed when EER_hard drops to 0.2 or below. Fits run in training mode neither emit nor mark the entity, so the first live fit reports it.
profile.separability is left untouched for unscored entities, which have fewer than 9 windows or are not part of a fit. NaN is never written into the dataclass float.

Device LR is defined as LR(t) = [(1-eps) p_A(t) + eps f(t)] / f(t), with eps = 0.05 (stack change on re-addressing), f = max(system share, rho = 0.02), share-weighted over B's stacks. A new or foreign stack gives LR = eps = 0.05 <= 0.1. NaN (no evidence) when A has no entity model.client or B has no stacks.
possible_impersonation fires when the log-odds without the device term is >= 5 with margin 2 over B's other candidates, and device LLR <= ln 0.1. It fires once per (B, A) pair, at MEDIUM severity.

Candidate restriction: same DHCP scope when B is in a configured scope; else the same B02 pool when B has one; else the whole system (the topology prior then separates /24s). Also required: gap <= 7 d, no active outgoing link, and at most 8 candidates by a cheap prior (topology + time + capped Gaussian).

Shared IP: the fit uses PCA(<= 4) of the centred zi rows (NaN -> 0, clipped at +-8; zi is already in z units) and a deterministic EM for the 2-component diagonal mixture, started from the PC1 median split. sklearn GaussianMixture measured ~50 ms per run at 96x4, against the spec's ~2 ms. Other details: first run needs >= 64 rows; runs are phased per entity with entity_due; both component weights must be >= 0.15; the local-hour histogram overlap must be >= 0.3; 'disjoint stacks' means different ja3n AND different UA family/major, with episodes within 300 s (B09's rule) on >= 2 ticks of the lookback; 3 negative runs clear the flag. Measured: bimodal delta >= 28 at 64 rows and >= 63 at 96; unimodal max -10.

Retraction applies only to links younger than ROLLBACK_MAX_DEPTH_S (7 d), and only when B was seen within the last hour. Older links are treated as the address being reused. link_retracted is emitted on B only, at LOW.
Actors include single-link components (a 2-member actor for a plain DHCP move), so B13 and B27 get the pair immediately.
Event severities chosen (the spec gives none): entity_resolution INFO, identity_moved INFO, shared_ip INFO (generator L7), possible_impersonation MEDIUM, link_retracted LOW.
